f.title: Base the extent of safety monitoring on a risk assessment
f.statement: The nature and extent of participant safety monitoring should be based on a risk assessment of the trial intervention(s), the stage of the trial and the extent of knowledge about the investigational products.
f.applicability: All clinical trials (medicines and devices)
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Risk management & minimisation

rows.quote: The nature and extent of participant safety monitoring should be based on a risk assessment of the trial intervention(s), the stage of the trial, and the extent of knowledge about the investigational products being tested.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, level and actor.

f.title: Sponsor holds overall responsibility for ongoing safety monitoring of the investigational product
f.statement: The trial sponsor has overall responsibility for the ongoing safety monitoring and evaluation of an investigational product, and should establish appropriate safety monitoring processes based on the potential risks, size and complexity of the trial.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: The trial sponsor has overall responsibility for the ongoing safety monitoring and evaluation of an investigational product. Trial sponsors should establish appropriate safety monitoring processes based on the potential risks, size and complexity of a particular trial.
rows.review_note: Review: level Mandatory for the statement of overall responsibility; process establishment is 'should'. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Document safety monitoring processes in the trial protocol
f.statement: Safety monitoring processes should be clearly documented in the trial protocol, including the assessment and management of risk (if not in another document), safety reporting definitions, procedures, responsibilities and reporting timelines, and any serious adverse events that do not require immediate reporting.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: Safety monitoring processes should be clearly documented in the trial protocol, including information on:
rows.review_note: Review: quote is the lead-in; content items are the bullets that follow. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Evaluate all available safety information and share it between non-commercial sponsor and manufacturer
f.statement: Trial sponsors should evaluate all safety information available to them, including investigator reports and other sources. In non-commercially sponsored trials, safety information should be shared between the non-commercial sponsor and the manufacturer/supplier of the investigational product so both satisfy their safety responsibilities.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Partner & vendor oversight

rows.quote:
Trial sponsors should evaluate all safety information that is available to them, including information reported by investigators and safety information from other sources. In the case of non-
commercially sponsored trials, it is important that safety information is shared between the non-
commercial sponsor and the manufacturer/supplier of the investigational product in order to ensure both parties satisfy their safety responsibilities.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, level and actor.

f.title: Use an independent committee or individuals to review accruing safety data
f.statement: To ensure appropriate independent oversight of trial safety, trial sponsors should generally use an independent committee (e.g. an IDMC) or independent individuals (e.g. a medical monitor) to review accruing safety data.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: To ensure there is appropriate independent oversight of clinical trial safety, trial sponsors should generally utilise an independent committee (eg, an Independent Data Monitoring Committee [IDMC]) or independent individuals (eg, a medical monitor) to review accruing safety data.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, level and actor.

f.title: Assess and categorise ICSRs received from investigators
f.statement: Trial sponsors should assess and categorise ICSRs received from investigators (e.g. assessing seriousness, causality, expectedness and categorising SUSARs) and ensure reportable ICSRs are reported to Medsafe.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: assess and categorise the ICSRs received from investigators (eg, assessing seriousness, causality, expectedness and categorising SUSARs) • ensure that any reportable ICSRs are reported to Medsafe

f.title: Produce safety communications and notify SSIs/USMs with impact clarified
f.statement: Trial sponsors should produce safety communications based on emerging safety data and IDMC/medical monitor feedback, notify investigators, Medsafe and HDEC of significant safety issues and urgent safety measures, and clarify the impact on participant safety, trial conduct or trial documentation when communicating safety information.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: produce safety communications based on emerging safety data and feedback from IDMCs/medical monitors • notify investigators, Medsafe, and HDEC of SSIs/USMs • clarify the impact of the information on participant safety, trial conduct or trial documentation when communicating safety information to investigators, Medsafe, and HDEC
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, level and actor.

f.title: Keep records of all local AEs and worldwide SUSARs with up-to-date line listings
f.statement: Trial sponsors should keep detailed records of all local adverse events and all worldwide SUSARs and maintain up-to-date tabulations and/or line listings to provide to Medsafe if requested.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Clinical safety monitoring

f.title: Sponsor may delegate safety reporting to third parties
f.statement: Trial sponsors may delegate reporting responsibilities to third parties, for example a coordinating centre; while pharmacovigilance functions may be outsourced, the sponsor retains overall responsibility for safety monitoring and reporting.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: Trial sponsors may delegate reporting responsibilities to third parties, for example, to a coordinating centre.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, level and actor.

f.title: Investigators: report SAEs, pregnancy birth defects and site USMs to the sponsor within 24 hours
f.statement: Investigators should capture and assess all AEs at the site per protocol, and report to the trial sponsor within 24 hours of becoming aware: all SAEs (except those identified in the protocol as not needing immediate reporting), any congenital anomaly/birth defect arising from any pregnancy of a participant or partner, and all USMs instigated by the site. Safety-critical AEs and requested information on deaths are reported as specified in the protocol.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

rows.deadline: Within 24 hours of becoming aware of the event
rows.quote: Report to the trial sponsor within 24 hours of becoming aware of the event:

f.title: Report fatal or life-threatening NZ SUSARs to Medsafe within 15 calendar days
f.statement: Expedited reporting to Medsafe of ICSRs is required for all fatal or life-threatening SUSARs occurring in New Zealand trial participants where the treatment is known (a decision has been made to unblind). The trial sponsor should submit these within 15 calendar days of becoming aware of the event, except where the Box 1 pharmacovigilance-system provision applies.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981
f.exceptions: Sponsors meeting Box 1 (established post-market PV system holding worldwide safety information) may choose not to submit expedited SUSARs after notifying Medsafe.

f.title: Keep blinding for all others involved in trial conduct and analysis
f.statement: Blinding should be maintained for all other persons involved in the conduct or management of the trial, including those responsible for data analysis and/or interpretation of results.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: Blinding should be maintained for all other persons involved in the conduct or management of the trial, including those responsible for data analysis and/or interpretation of results.

f.title: Hold non-fatal NZ SUSARs in accessible form, available on request
f.statement: All other ICSRs of SUSARs occurring in New Zealand participants that are not fatal or life-threatening should not be routinely reported to Medsafe but must be held in an accessible form and made available on request.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Clinical safety monitoring

All other ICSRs of SUSARs occurring in New Zealand trial participants that are not fatal or life-

f.title: Do not downgrade the investigator's causality; send both opinions with the SUSAR
f.statement: If the sponsor's causality assessment conflicts with the investigator's, the investigator's assessment cannot be downgraded by the sponsor (from 'related' to 'not related'). If the investigator's judgement triggers a SUSAR, the opinions of both investigator and sponsor are provided with the SUSAR report sent to Medsafe.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: the investigator’s assessment cannot be downgraded by the trial sponsor (ie, altered from ‘related’ to ‘not related’). In this case, if an investigator’s judgment triggers the reporting of a SUSAR, provide the opinion of both the investigator and the trial sponsor with any SUSAR report sent to Medsafe.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source; no change. Double-check: quote proves statement, level and actor.

f.title: Sponsor retains overall responsibility when outsourcing PV
f.statement: While pharmacovigilance functions may be outsourced to a third party, the trial sponsor retains overall responsibility for safety monitoring and reporting.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

f.title: Box 1: sponsors with an established PV system may opt out of expedited SUSAR reports
f.statement: Trial sponsors with established post-market pharmacovigilance systems used to monitor the investigational product may choose not to submit expedited SUSAR reports to Medsafe, only where the sponsor holds all relevant (worldwide) safety information. The system should be consistent with international GVP and include PV expertise, a quality system, a PV database for receiving, analysing and reporting ICSRs, the ability to identify new signals or trends, and the ability to produce DSURs.
f.clause: 4.1.1 Box 1 - When there is a pharmacovigilance system
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: Trial sponsors with established post-market pharmacovigilance systems that will be used to monitor the safety of the investigational product may choose not to submit expedited reports of SUSARs to Medsafe. This applies only where the trial sponsor holds all relevant safety information (ie, worldwide) for the investigational product, as these sponsors are best placed to perform an analysis of these reports.

f.title: Box 1: notify Medsafe of the intention not to submit expedited SUSARs, with a PV system overview
f.statement: Where the Box 1 requirements are met, once the trial is approved, notify Medsafe by email of the intention not to submit expedited SUSAR reports for the trial (at any time after approval), providing an overview or executive summary of the pharmacovigilance system with the initial notification. Notify Medsafe when subsequent trials use the same system, and of significant changes to the system.

f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

f.title: Decide in advance how active-comparator AEs are reported; avoid duplicate reporting
f.statement: For AEs associated with another supplier's medicine used as an active comparator, the trial sponsor should decide in advance whether such events are reported to the other manufacturer/supplier and/or directly to Medsafe; duplicated reporting to Medsafe should be avoided.
f.clause: 4.1 Reporting adverse events/individual case safety reports
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: For AEs associated with another supplier or manufacturer’s medicine that is used as an active comparator in a clinical trial, the trial sponsor should decide in advance whether such events should be reported to the other manufacturer/supplier and/or directly to Medsafe. Duplicated reporting to Medsafe (ie, reporting of the same event by both the sponsor and other supplier or manufacturer) should be avoided.

f.title: Report AEs to approved concomitant/rescue medicines per the PV guideline
f.statement: Adverse events associated with approved medicines used during a trial (e.g. concomitant or rescue medicines) should be reported as outlined in GRTPNZ: Pharmacovigilance. Events associated with placebo will not usually meet the criteria for reporting.
f.clause: 4.1 Reporting adverse events/individual case safety reports
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: Adverse events associated with approved medicines used during a trial (eg, concomitant medicines, rescue medicines) should be reported as outlined in GRTPNZ: Pharmacovigilance

f.title: Hold reports of all NZ AEs and overseas SUSARs in accessible form, available on request
f.statement: Medsafe expects the trial sponsor to hold reports of all AEs occurring in New Zealand participants; these should not be routinely reported (except as in 4.1.1) but must be held in an accessible form and made available on request. ICSRs of SUSARs at overseas sites should likewise not be routinely reported but must be held and made available on request.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote: Medsafe expects the trial sponsor to hold reports of all AEs occurring in New Zealand participants. f.title: Submit reportable ICSRs per GRTPNZ: Pharmacovigilance and include the protocol number
f.statement: Reportable ICSRs are submitted to Medsafe using the methods in section 4.4 of GRTPNZ: Pharmacovigilance, including the trial protocol number in the report; they may also be submitted via Ethics RM (SCOTT post-approval form).
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

f.title: Notify significant safety issues to Medsafe within 15 calendar days
f.statement: Significant safety issues (SSIs) are notified to Medsafe within 15 calendar days of the trial sponsor's awareness of the issue. The notification should include details of the issue (including similar issues at overseas sites) and proposed actions; for a temporary halt or early termination for safety reasons, the reasons, scope, measures taken and further actions planned, and arrangements for the NZ arm if halted overseas.
f.clause: 4.2 Reporting significant safety issues/urgent safety measures
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

f.title: Obtain approval from Medsafe and HDEC before restarting a halted trial
f.statement: If a trial is being restarted after a temporary halt, notify Medsafe and the HDEC before restart; approval is required before the study can restart.
f.clause: 4.2 Reporting significant safety issues/urgent safety measures
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

f.title: Report urgent safety measures to Medsafe and HDEC within 7 calendar days
f.statement: Urgent safety measures may be instigated before notification but must be reported to Medsafe and the HDEC as soon as possible and no later than 7 calendar days after taking them, via Ethics RM or by email to Medsafe.
f.clause: 4.2 Reporting significant safety issues/urgent safety measures
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

f.title: Submit an annual safety report (DSUR acceptable) to Medsafe
f.statement: Submit a safety report each year to Medsafe. If available, the DSUR can be the safety report (the executive summary is acceptable, with the full DSUR available on request); a DSUR from other jurisdictions is acceptable and its timing may be aligned with global cycles.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

f.title: Content of the annual safety report when no DSUR is available
f.statement: If a DSUR is not available, the annual safety report should generally include a brief description and analysis of new and relevant safety findings; of the safety profile and its implications for participants; a discussion of implications for the trial's risks and benefits; and a description of measures taken or proposed to minimise risks.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

f.title: Submit the annual safety report to HDEC with the annual progress report (max two pages, lay language)
f.statement: Submit the annual safety report to HDEC with the annual progress report (every 12 months from the date of approval) through Ethics RM. The HDEC report must be no longer than two pages and written in lay language, should include a brief analysis of new findings, implications for the risk-benefit ratio and risk-minimising measures, and should not include line listings.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.deadline: Every 12 months from the date of approval

f.title: Submit protocol amendments to Medsafe and substantial amendments to HDEC before implementation
f.statement: Protocol amendments (including safety-related ones) should be submitted to Medsafe as detailed in GRTPNZ: Clinical Trials. Substantial amendments are submitted to HDEC for approval before implementation; substantial protocol deviations, including serious or significant adverse findings in for-cause audit reports, must be notified to HDEC in a timely manner.
f.applicability: Clinical trials of medicines approved under section 30 of the Medicines Act 1981

rows.quote: Protocol amendments (including safety-related amendments) should be submitted to Medsafe, as detailed in GRTPNZ: Clinical Trials (available on the Medsafe website).
